speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I need to understand your skin concerns to determine if there are any oncologic implications. What specific changes, such as new growths or sores, have you noticed on your skin?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for sharing those details. Given the non-healing nature of the lesions, your significant smoking history, and the unusual locations (penile shaft and finger), I need to know if you have noticed any bleeding, pain, or change in the size or shape of these spots recently.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) to check for anemia or infection.

REQUEST IMAGES: If you have any photos of the lesions, please provide them for my review.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The CBC results are normal, which is helpful. Regarding the lesions on your penis and finger, have you noticed any ulceration, bleeding, or a "hard" indurated feel to them? Additionally, do you have a history of HPV infection or other sexually transmitted diseases?

REQUEST TEST: Serum SCA (Squamous Cell Carcinoma Antigen) levels.
REQUEST IMAGES: Please describe the color, borders, and surface texture of the lesions in detail if photos are unavailable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal CBC and SCA results are helpful, but your history of heavy smoking and non-healing lesions in sun-exposed and mucosal areas is concerning. Have you noticed the lesions are firm, raised, or have rolled edges, and do you have any personal history of skin cancer?

REQUEST TEST: Tumor Markers (CEA, CA-19-9) to screen for metastatic potential.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC). The clinical presentation of non-healing, crusted lesions in high-risk areas (penile shaft, finger) combined with a 30-year history of heavy smoking and unsuccessful prior treatments for syphilis/eczema strongly indicates malignancy. Normal tumor markers and CBC do not rule out localized SCC. Further biopsy is clinically mandated to confirm the diagnosis and stage the disease.
